Base directory for this skill: D:\code\codeflow\.claude\skills\cook # Cook - Smart Feature Implementation End-to-end implementation with automatic workflow detection. **Principles:** YAGNI, KISS, DRY | Token efficiency | Concise reports ## Usage ``` /ck:cook ``` **IMPORTANT:** If no flag is provided, the skill will use the `interactive` mode by default for the workflow. **Optional flags to select the workflow mode:** - `--interactive`: Full workflow with user input (**default**) - `--fast`: Skip research, scout→plan→code - `--parallel`: Multi-agent execution - `--no-test`: Skip testing step - `--auto`: Auto-approve all steps **Composable flags** (combine with any mode): - `--tdd`: Tests-first per phase — write tests for current behavior before refactoring, then verify they still pass after the implementation step **Example:** ``` /ck:cook "Add user authentication to the app" --fast /ck:cook path/to/plan.md --auto /ck:cook "Refactor auth middleware" --tdd ``` Do NOT write implementation code until a plan exists and has been reviewed. This applies regardless of task simplicity. "Simple" tasks are where unexamined assumptions waste the most time. Exception: `--fast` mode skips research but still requires a plan step. User override: If user explicitly says "just code it" or "skip planning", respect their instruction. Before planning OR asking clarifying questions, scan the codebase. Mandatory scout outputs: 1. Project type, language(s), framework(s) 2. Existing modules/files relevant to the task 3. Current patterns/conventions for similar features (so the implementation matches them) 4. Existing docs in `./docs/` and any in-flight plans in `./plans/` covering this area 5. Public APIs, schemas, contracts that the task could affect State a 3-6 bullet codebase-context summary to the user before asking questions. Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path (the plan already encodes scout output). Before producing a plan, you MUST be able to answer ALL of these in one concrete sentence each (use `AskUserQuestion` to pin them down — do NOT proceed on vague intent): 1. **Expected output**: the concrete artifact(s) the user will see at the end (file paths, feature behavior, UI screen, API endpoint + payload, CLI command + flags). 2. **Acceptance criteria**: specific behaviors / inputs → outputs / edge cases that MUST work to call it "done". 3. **Scope boundary**: what is explicitly OUT of scope this round. 4. **Non-negotiable constraints**: stack, file locations, naming, backward compatibility, deadlines, performance. 5. **Touchpoints**: which existing files/modules (from scout) will be modified or extended; which contracts must stay stable. Ground every `AskUserQuestion` option in scout findings (e.g., "Add to `src/api/users.ts` (matches existing pattern) or new `src/api/profile.ts`?"). Skip ONLY when input is a `plan.md`/`phase-*.md` path. Implementation is NOT done until verified to be side-effect-free. Code-review and test gates MUST prove: 1. New behavior matches every acceptance criterion above. 2. All tests pass — including tests in modules that share files/contracts with the change. 3. No existing business logic / workflow regression: explicitly walk each touchpoint and any caller of changed functions. 4. No new lint/type/build errors anywhere in the repo. 5. Public contracts unchanged unless intentional and called out (function signatures, exported types, API responses, DB schemas, env vars, config keys). User override: If user invoked `--no-test`, item 2 is downgraded to a warning. Surface the unverified-tests risk in the finalize `AskUserQuestion` so the user accepts the trade-off rather than having it silently chosen. Items 1, 3, 4, 5 remain enforceable via the mandatory `code-reviewer` subagent. If review/testing reveals a side effect, regression, or broken workflow, STOP. Use `AskUserQuestion` to present: - What broke (file, test, workflow, user-facing behavior) - Why this implementation caused it (1-line cause) - 2-4 concrete options for the user to choose, e.g.: - "Revert this slice and re-plan with stricter scope" - "Keep the implementation and update to match the new contract" - "Add a compatibility shim at so old callers keep working" - "Accept the regression — old behavior was unintended/buggy" Let the user decide. Do not silently patch around regressions. ## Anti-Rationalization | Thought | Reality | |---------|---------| | "This is too simple to plan" | Simple tasks have hidden complexity. Plan takes 30 seconds. | | "I already know how to do this" | Knowing ≠ planning. Write it down. | | "Let me just start coding" | Undisciplined action wastes tokens. Plan first. | | "The user wants speed" | Fastest path = plan → implement → done. Not: implement → debug → rewrite. | | "I'll plan as I go" | That's not planning, that's hoping. | | "Just this once" | Every skip is "just this once." No exceptions. | ## Smart Intent Detection | Input Pattern | Detected Mode | Behavior | |---------------|---------------|----------| | Path to `plan.md` or `phase-*.md` | code | Execute existing plan | | Contains "fast", "quick" | fast | Skip research, scout→plan→code | | Contains "trust me", "auto" | auto | Auto-approve all steps | | Lists 3+ features OR "parallel" | parallel | Multi-agent execution | | Contains "no test", "skip test" | no-test | Skip testing step | | Default | interactive | Full workflow with user input | See `references/intent-detection.md` for detection logic. ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Intent Detection] --> B{Has plan path?} B -->|Yes| F[Load Plan] B -->|No| C{Mode?} C -->|fast| D[Scout → Plan → Code] C -->|interactive/auto| SC[Scout Codebase MANDATORY] SC --> SR[Summarize Findings to User] SR --> RQ{Exact requirements captured?
output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints} RQ -->|No| SR RQ -->|Yes| E[Research → Review → Plan] E --> F D --> F F --> G[Review Gate] G -->|approved| H[Implement] G -->|rejected| E H --> H1{Simplify signal?} H1 -->|Yes| H2[Conditional Simplify] H1 -->|No| I[Review Gate] H2 --> I I -->|approved| J{--no-test?} J -->|No| K[Test] J -->|Yes| L[Finalize] K --> L L --> M[Report + Journal] ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** Prose sections below provide detail for each node. If prose conflicts with this flow, follow the diagram. ## Workflow Overview ``` [Intent Detection] → [Research?] → [Review] → [Plan] → [Review] → [Implement] → [Conditional Simplify?] → [Review] → [Test?] → [Review] → [Finalize] ``` **Default (non-auto):** Stops at `[Review]` gates for human approval before each major step. **Auto mode (`--auto`):** Skips human review gates, implements all phases continuously. **Claude Tasks:** Utilize `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskGet`, `TaskList` during implementation step. **Fallback:** These are CLI-only tools — unavailable in VSCode extension. If they error, use `TodoWrite` for progress tracking instead. | Mode | Research | Testing | Review Gates | Phase Progression | |------|----------|---------|--------------|-------------------| | interactive | ✓ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | auto | ✓ | ✓ | Auto if score≥9.5 | All at once (no stops) | | fast | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | parallel | Optional | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Parallel groups | | no-test | ✓ | ✗ | **User approval at each step** | One at a time | | code | ✗ | ✓ | **User approval at each step** | Per plan | ## Step Output Format ``` ✓ Step [N]: [Brief status] - [Key metrics] ``` ## Blocking Gates (Non-Auto Mode) Human review required at these checkpoints (skipped with `--auto`): - **Post-Research:** Review findings before planning - **Post-Plan:** Approve plan before implementation - **Post-Implementation:** Approve code before testing - **Post-Testing:** 100% pass + approve before finalize **Always enforced (all modes):** - **Testing:** 100% pass required (unless no-test mode) - **Code Review (MANDATORY):** Spawn `code-reviewer` subagent with explicit checks: (a) every acceptance criterion met, (b) no regression to business logic in touchpoints/blast-radius, (c) no breaking changes to public contracts (signatures, schemas, APIs, env vars) unless called out, (d) follows existing patterns from scout, (e) no new lint/type/build errors anywhere. Pass scout summary + acceptance criteria as context. If reviewer flags side effects → trigger HARD-GATE-NO-SIDE-EFFECTS (`AskUserQuestion` with 2-4 options). Then: User approval OR auto-approve (score≥9.5, 0 critical). - **Finalize (MANDATORY - never skip):** 1. **Activate `/ck:project-management` skill (MANDATORY)** → run full plan sync-back across ALL `phase-XX-*.md` (not only current phase), update `plan.md` status/progress, hydrate Claude Tasks, generate progress report 2. `docs-manager` subagent → update `./docs` if changes warrant 3. `TaskUpdate` → mark all Claude Tasks complete after sync-back verification (skip if Task tools unavailable) 4. Ask user if they want to commit via `git-manager` subagent 5. Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion ## Required Subagents (MANDATORY) | Phase | Subagent | Requirement | |-------|----------|-------------| | Research | `researcher` | Optional in fast/code | | Scout | `ck:scout` | Optional in code | | Plan | `planner` | Optional in code | | UI Work | `ui-ux-designer` | If frontend work | | Testing | `tester`, `debugger` | **MUST** spawn | | Review | `code-reviewer` | **MUST** spawn | | Finalize | `/ck:project-management` skill + `docs-manager`, `git-manager` subagents | **MUST** invoke all | **CRITICAL ENFORCEMENT:** - Steps 4, 5, 6 **MUST** use Task tool to spawn subagents - DO NOT implement testing, review, or finalization yourself - DELEGATE - If workflow ends with 0 Task tool calls, it is INCOMPLETE - Pattern: `Task(subagent_type="[type]", prompt="[task]", description="[brief]")` ## References - `references/intent-detection.md` - Detection rules and routing logic - `references/workflow-steps.md` - Detailed step definitions for all modes - `references/review-cycle.md` - Interactive and auto review processes - `references/subagent-patterns.md` - Subagent invocation patterns ## Workflow Position **Typically follows:** `/ck:plan` (execute a plan), `/ck:brainstorm` (implement agreed solution) **Typically precedes:** `/ck:code-review` (review after implementation), `/ck:test` (validate changes) **Related:** `/ck:fix` (alternative for bug fixes), `/ck:plan` (create plan before cooking) ARGUMENTS: D:\code\codeflow\plans\260603-7phase-provenance-cost-quality-compliance

# CODEFLOW — AI Code Supply Chain OS

## Overview

Transform RTK (`D:/code/invesments/tools_decisions/rtk-analysis/`) from a token compression CLI into an **AI Code Supply Chain Operating System** answering 4 questions: WHO wrote it, WHAT did it cost, IS it safe, CAN you prove it.

**Codebase reality check:** RTK is 105 .rs files, ~69K LOC. Key assets to extend:
- `tracking.rs` (1689 LOC) — SQLite tracking, RTK compression savings (NOT LLM API tokens)
- `ccusage.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` — Claude Code spending data parsing (actual API billing — authoritative cost source)

- `discover/rules.rs` (935 LOC) — static command-rewrite table (`RtkRule` maps CLI → RTK proxies). NOT an extensible rule engine.
- `build.rs` (66 LOC) — **already exists** (Windows stack size + TOML filter concatenation). Must extend, not create.
- `filters/` — 59+ TOML-based output filters

**What does NOT exist yet:** protobuf schema, provenance records, signed attestation, PostToolUse hooks (must be built from scratch), budget policy engine, dependency validation, compliance exports.

**Descoped:** Cloud backend (Go + ClickHouse + NATS + Next.js) moved to separate future plan — too large for this plan's scope. Phase 6 replaced with lightweight CLI export + optional SQLite-based dashboard.

**Target:** 10-week MVP across 7 phases. Phases 1-5 = CLI (Rust). Phase 6 = CLI export + lightweight dashboard. Phase 7 = Launch.

# Phase 3: Budget Governance + Policy Engine

## Overview

Real-time budget enforcement in PreToolUse hooks. Policy engine evaluates per-dev, per-project, per-team spending limits and can warn or block tool calls that exceed budget. Model downgrade is NOT supported (hook protocol has no model_id in response).

## Requirements

- Functional: TOML-based policy definitions (per-dev, per-project, per-team limits); PreToolUse budget check (warn/block only — no downgrade); alert webhooks on threshold breach; `codeflow budget` CLI for status/policy management
- Non-functional: policy evaluation <2ms; fail-open if policy engine errors; policies hot-reloadable without restart

## Architecture

**Critical constraints (from red-team):**
1. Hooks are opt-in — developer can remove hook from settings → budget enforcement disappears. This is an inherent local-first limitation. Real enforcement requires API key proxy (future cloud phase).
2. Hook protocol does NOT support model_id in response — Downgrade verdict is impossible. Verdicts are Warn or Block only.

```
PreToolUse hook → read accumulated cost for {dev, project} from tracking.db
    ↓
PolicyEngine.evaluate(context) → Verdict { Allow | Warn(msg) | Block(reason) }
    ↓
If Block → return error JSON to agent (tool call rejected)
If Warn → log warning to stderr, allow tool call
    ↓
GovernanceEvent { policy_id, action, reason, budget_remaining, developer_id }
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_GOVERNANCE → queued for export
```

66

68	
69	```
70	Claude Code → PreToolUse hook → codeflow processes → compressed/deduped output

72

74	- ANSI codes, download progress bars, empty lines

# CODEFLOW

**AI coding cost intelligence engine.** Reduce token costs 40-65% while proving developer productivity is maintained.

CODEFLOW intercepts AI coding tool output, compresses it via smart filters, deduplicates repeated reads, and tracks savings — all with <5ms overhead.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Install
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codeflow-dev/codeflow/main/install.sh | sh

# Or with cargo
cargo install --git https://github.com/codeflow-dev/codeflow codeflow --root ~/.local

# Set up hooks for Claude Code
codeflow init

# View your savings
codeflow stats
```

## Demo Setup

Run the full stack locally with seed data (requires Docker):

```bash
# Start all services (ClickHouse, NATS, API, Dashboard)
docker compose up -d

# Seed demo data (570 events, 14 days, 3 projects)
docker compose --profile seed up seed

# Open dashboard
open http://localhost:3000
```

### CLI + Live Sync Demo

```bash
# Install hooks in any project
codeflow init

# Run some commands (savings tracked automatically)
codeflow wrap git status
codeflow wrap cargo test

# View local savings
codeflow stats

# Sync to cloud dashboard
CODEFLOW_API_URL=http://localhost:8080 codeflow sync --once
```

### Ports

| Service | Port |
|---------|------|
| Dashboard | 3000 |
| API | 8080 |
| ClickHouse HTTP | 8123 |
| ClickHouse Native | 9000 |
| NATS | 4222 |

## How It Works

CODEFLOW installs as a Claude Code hook that intercepts **all major tool calls** — Bash, Read, Grep, and Glob:

```
Claude Code → PreToolUse hook → codeflow processes → compressed/deduped output
```

**Layer 1 — Compression:** An 8-stage TOML filter pipeline strips noise from Bash command output:
- ANSI codes, download progress bars, empty lines
- Verbose compiler/test output condensed to errors + summary
- Long outputs truncated with head/tail

**Layer 2 — Dedup:** Content-addressed cache detects repeated Bash command output within a session and returns a one-line summary instead of full content.

**Layer 2.5 — Read Dedup:** Intercepts Read/Grep/Glob tool calls. If a file was recently read and hasn't changed (mtime verified), injects `additionalContext` telling Claude the file is unchanged — saving 30-50% of session tokens from re-reads.

# Phase 1: Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core

## Overview

Establish event schema (protobuf), content hashing (blake3), signed attestation (Ed25519), and the `codeflow blame` CLI command. This phase creates the data foundation all other pillars depend on.

## Requirements

- Functional: capture code hash, file paths, contributor type via diff-on-next-PreToolUse pattern (no PostToolUse exists); model_id enriched retroactively from ccusage; sign provenance records with Ed25519; export Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON; `codeflow blame` command shows line-by-line AI attribution
- Non-functional: <5ms hook latency (fail-open); provenance DB <50MB for 90 days typical usage; zero network dependency for local operation

## Architecture

**Critical constraint:** Only PreToolUse hooks exist. PostToolUse does NOT exist in any agent's hook protocol. Each hook invocation is a separate OS process — no shared in-memory state. Hook JSON payload contains only `tool_name` + `tool_input.command` — no `model_id`.

```
PreToolUse hook (tool N) → snapshot working tree state (file hashes)
    ↓ (agent executes tool, modifies files)
PreToolUse hook (tool N+1) → diff working tree vs snapshot → detect changes from tool N
    ↓
ProvenanceRecord { model_id: "unknown"/enriched, code_hash, file_path, lines, attestation_sig }
    ↓
SQLite (extend tracking.db, WAL mode) ← single DB, no split-brain
    ↓
Protobuf event → EVENT_TYPE_PROVENANCE → queued for export
```

**Provenance capture strategy:** Since PostToolUse doesn't exist, use "diff-on-next-PreToolUse" pattern:
1. Each PreToolUse: read last snapshot from DB, diff current working tree against it, record changes as provenance from previous tool call
2. Store new snapshot for next comparison
3. Fallback: `codeflow blame --retroactive` scans git history for attribution after the fact

**model_id enrichment:** Hook JSON has no model_id. Strategies:
1. Parse from ccusage session data (retroactive, but accurate)
2. Infer from agent config files (`.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/config.json`)
3. Accept "unknown" as valid — enrich later when data available

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — add provenance snapshot capture to PreToolUse handlers (no PostToolUse exists)
- Modify: `src/hooks/mod.rs` — export new provenance module
- Modify: `src/core/mod.rs` — export provenance module
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `blame` subcommand
- Modify: `Cargo.toml` — add prost, prost-build, ed25519-dalek, blake3 deps
- Create: `proto/events.proto` — protobuf schema for all 7 event types
- Modify: `build.rs` — extend existing build.rs with prost-build compilation of proto files (DO NOT create new — existing handles Windows stack size + TOML filter concat)
- Create: `src/core/provenance.rs` — ProvenanceRecord struct, signing, storage
- Create: `src/core/attestation.rs` — Ed25519 key management, sign/verify
- Create: `src/core/content_hash.rs` — blake3 hashing for code content
- Create: `src/core/agent_trace.rs` — Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export format
- Create: `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs` — `codeflow blame` command implementation

## Implementation Steps

1. **Add dependencies to Cargo.toml**
   - `prost = "0.13"`, `prost-types = "0.13"` (runtime)
   - `prost-build = "0.13"` (build-dependency)
   - `ed25519-dalek = { version = "2", features = ["rand_core"] }`
   - `blake3 = "1"`
   - `rand = "0.8"` (for key generation)

2. **Create `proto/events.proto`**
   - Define EventType enum (7 types per brainstorm §3.4)
   - Define ProvenanceEvent, CostEvent, GovernanceEvent, QualityEvent messages
   - Define EventEnvelope wrapper with timestamp, event_type, oneof payload

3. **Extend existing `build.rs`** (66 LOC — has Windows `/STACK:8388608` + TOML filter concat)
   - Add prost-build to compile proto/events.proto → src/proto/mod.rs
   - Preserve existing Windows stack size config and filter concatenation logic
   - Add to .gitignore: generated proto output (or check in — decide)

4. **Create `src/core/content_hash.rs`**
   - `fn hash_content(content: &[u8]) -> String` — blake3 hash, hex-encoded
   - `fn hash_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String>` — hash file contents
   - `fn hash_diff(old: &str, new: &str) -> String` — hash the diff

5. **Create `src/core/attestation.rs`**
   - `struct KeyPair` — wraps Ed25519 keypair
   - `fn generate_keypair() -> KeyPair` — auto-generate, store at `dirs::data_dir()/rtk/keys/` (cross-platform via `dirs` crate, already in Cargo.toml)
   - `fn load_or_generate() -> Result<KeyPair>` — lazy init
   - `fn sign(keypair: &KeyPair, data: &[u8]) -> String` — hex-encoded signature
   - `fn verify(pubkey: &[u8], data: &[u8], sig: &str) -> bool`

6. **Create `src/core/provenance.rs`**
   - `struct ProvenanceRecord` — model_id (default "unknown", enriched later), model_version, prompt_hash, code_hash, file_path, start_line, end_line, contributor_type (human|ai|mixed|unknown), attestation_sig, timestamp, developer_id, session_id
   - `struct ProvenanceStore` — SQLite-backed, **extend tracking.db** (single DB — no split-brain)
   - `fn record_provenance(...)` — insert record + sign with attestation
   - `fn query_by_file(path: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>` — for blame command
   - `fn query_by_session(session_id: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>`
   - `fn enrich_model_id(session_id: &str, model_id: &str)` — retroactive enrichment from ccusage
   - Schema: `CREATE TABLE provenance_records (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, model_id TEXT DEFAULT 'unknown', ...)`

7. **Extend `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`** (PreToolUse ONLY — no PostToolUse exists)
   - In PreToolUse handler: before processing current tool, diff working tree against last snapshot
   - If changes detected since last snapshot → create ProvenanceRecord for PREVIOUS tool's changes
   - Compute blake3 hash of changed files, sign with Ed25519, store in tracking.db
   - Update snapshot in DB for next PreToolUse comparison
   - model_id: default to "unknown" (enriched later via `codeflow blame --enrich`)
   - Fail-open: if provenance capture fails, log warning but don't block the tool call
   - NOTE: each hook invocation is a separate OS process — all state must go through SQLite, not in-memory

8. **Create `src/core/agent_trace.rs`**
   - Implement Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON format (per github.com/cursor/agent-trace spec)
   - `fn to_agent_trace(record: &ProvenanceRecord) -> Value` — convert to spec JSON
   - `fn export_agent_trace(records: Vec<ProvenanceRecord>) -> String` — full trace file

9. **Create `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow blame <file>` — line-by-line attribution
   - Output format: `<line_num> | <contributor> | <model_id> | <timestamp> | <code>`
   - Color-coded: human=green, ai=yellow, mixed=cyan, unknown=gray
   - Flag: `--json` for machine-readable output
   - Flag: `--session <id>` to filter by session

10. **Wire into main.rs**
    - Add `Blame` variant to Commands enum
    - Route to blame_cmd handler

11. **Tests**
    - Unit: content_hash (known vectors), attestation (sign/verify roundtrip), provenance (CRUD)
    - Integration: mock PreToolUse JSON + file changes → verify provenance record created via diff-on-next-PreToolUse
    - CLI: `codeflow blame` on test fixture files

## Success Criteria

- [x] `proto/events.proto` compiles with prost-build, generates Rust types
- [x] Ed25519 keypair auto-generated on first use, persisted at `dirs::data_dir()/rtk/keys/` (cross-platform)
- [x] ProvenanceRecord created for file changes via diff-on-next-PreToolUse pattern
- [x] `codeflow blame <file>` shows line-by-line AI attribution with model_id
- [x] Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export passes format validation
- [x] Hook latency addressed (mtime pre-filter + RTK_PROVENANCE=0 opt-out)
- [x] Existing RTK tests still pass (2012 passed, 0 failed, no regression)
- [x] 18 new tests for provenance, attestation, content_hash, agent_trace

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| model_id NOT available in hook JSON payload | HIGH | Default "unknown"; enrich retroactively from ccusage session data; infer from agent config |
| No PostToolUse hook exists | CRITICAL | Use diff-on-next-PreToolUse pattern; fallback to git-based retroactive analysis |
| prost-build adds Windows build complexity | MEDIUM | Use pre-generated .rs files as fallback; CI builds on Linux |
| build.rs already exists (66 LOC) | LOW | Extend existing file; preserve Windows stack size + TOML filter logic |
| Provenance DB grows too large | LOW | 90-day retention (reuse tracking.rs pattern); vacuum on startup |

## Security Considerations

- Ed25519 private key stored with 0600 permissions (Unix) or ACL-restricted (Windows)
- Never log private key material
- Attestation signatures are non-repudiable — document this for users
- Content hashes use blake3 (cryptographic) not xxhash (fast but not cryptographic)

## Code Review Summary

### Scope
- **Files**: 4 new modules (`content_hash.rs`, `attestation.rs`, `provenance.rs`, `agent_trace.rs`), 7 modified files (`main.rs`, `wrap.rs`, `sync.rs`, `events.rs`, `lib.rs`, `proto_generated.rs`, `events.proto`)
- **LOC**: ~850 new lines across 4 modules, ~120 lines changed in existing files
- **Focus**: Phase 1 provenance system -- Ed25519 attestation, provenance tracking, blame CLI, Agent Trace export
- **Tests**: 113/113 pass, 0 failures

### Overall Assessment
Solid foundation. The architecture is clean: content hashing, attestation, provenance storage, and trace export are properly separated. The diff-on-next-PreToolUse pattern is correctly implemented. The fail-open design ensures hook errors never block tool execution. Proto schema changes are additive-only as required. However, there are several issues ranging from a potential panic to security gaps on Windows.

---

### Critical Issues

**1. Panic on short `code_hash` in `handle_blame` (main.rs:226)**

```rust
&rec.code_hash[..12]
```

If `code_hash` is ever fewer than 12 bytes (e.g., corrupt DB row, empty string from a default), this panics with a byte-index-out-of-bounds. Since this is user-facing CLI output from DB data, it must be defensive.

**Fix:**
```rust
&rec.code_hash[..rec.code_hash.len().min(12)]
```

**2. Private key stored without ACL protection on Windows (attestation.rs:46-50)**

The `#[cfg(unix)]` block sets 0o600 on the private key file, but on Windows (which is a supported platform per the environment) there is no equivalent ACL restriction. Any local user can read the signing key from `%LOCALAPPDATA%/codeflow/keys/signing.key`.

**Impact**: Another process or user on the same machine can read the Ed25519 signing key and forge attestation signatures, undermining the entire provenance chain.

**Recommendation**: Add a `#[cfg(windows)]` block that restricts the ACL using the `windows-acl` crate or shell out to `icacls`. At minimum, document this as a known limitation.

**3. TOCTOU race in `load_or_generate` (attestation.rs:95-104)**

```rust
if key_path.exists() {
    KeyPair::load(&key_path)
} else {
    let kp = KeyPair::generate();
    kp.save(&key_path)?;
    Ok(kp)
}
```

If two concurrent hook invocations race (which happens -- each hook is a separate OS process), both may see `exists() == false`, both generate different keys, and the second `save` silently overwrites the first. Any provenance records signed by the first process now have a signature that cannot be verified against the persisted key.

**Recommendation**: Use `OpenOptions::create_new(true)` for atomic create-or-fail, then fall back to `load` on `AlreadyExists` error. This eliminates the race window.

---

### High Priority

**4. Fallback key directory is `/tmp` (attestation.rs:89)**

```rust
.unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("/tmp"))
```

If both `dirs::data_dir()` and `dirs::home_dir()` fail, the signing key is written to `/tmp/codeflow/keys/signing.key` which is world-readable on most systems. On a shared server, this leaks the private key.

**Recommendation**: Return an error instead of falling back to `/tmp`. A missing home directory is an exceptional condition that should fail loudly rather than silently storing keys in an insecure location.

**5. `now_ms()` casts `u128` to `i64` without overflow check (provenance.rs:378)**

```rust
.as_millis() as i64
```

`as_millis()` returns `u128`. Casting to `i64` silently truncates if the value exceeds `i64::MAX` (year ~292 million). While not practically reachable with real system clocks, this same pattern exists in the test helper `now_ms` in `events.rs` that returns `u64`, creating an inconsistency. Use `try_from` or at minimum be consistent across modules.

**6. Provenance DB opened on every hook invocation**

`capture_provenance` in `main.rs:318` opens a new SQLite connection (`ProvenanceStore::open`) and generates/loads keys (`load_or_generate`) on every `PreToolUse` hook call. Each hook is a separate OS process, so this means:
- One SQLite `open()` + WAL setup per tool call
- One filesystem read of `signing.key` per tool call
- One `get_all_snapshots` query per tool call

For a session with hundreds of tool calls, this adds measurable latency. The WAL mode and `busy_timeout=5000` mitigate contention, but the per-process overhead remains.

**Recommendation**: This is architecturally acceptable for Phase 1 since the fail-open pattern (`let _ = capture_provenance(...)`) ensures it never blocks. Worth noting for Phase 2 optimization -- a long-lived daemon or shared-memory approach would amortize these costs.

**7. `detect_changes` reads entire file content twice (provenance.rs:311, 320)**

```rust
let current_hash = match content_hash::hash_file(&abs_path) {  // reads file
    ...
};
let line_count = std::fs::read_to_string(&abs_path)  // reads file again
    .map(|s| s.lines().count() as u32)
    ...
```

For large files, this doubles I/O. `hash_file` already reads the full content; the line count could be computed from the same buffer.

---

### Medium Priority

**8. `ContributorType` defined in two places with divergent serialization**

`provenance.rs` defines `ContributorType` as a Rust enum with `as_str()` returning `"ai"`, `"human"`, etc. `proto_generated.rs` defines a proto `ContributorType` enum with `as_str_name()` returning `"CONTRIBUTOR_TYPE_AI"`, etc. These are not connected -- a conversion between them is missing, which will matter when provenance events flow through the proto sync path.

**9. `snapshot_files` uses `unwrap_or("")` for path conversion (provenance.rs:366)**

```rust
let mtime = crate::util::get_file_mtime_ns(abs_path.to_str().unwrap_or(""))
```

If the path contains non-UTF-8 characters (rare but possible on some filesystems), this silently passes an empty string and gets `mtime = 0`. Consider using `to_string_lossy()` or propagating the error.

**10. `handle_blame` has hardcoded ANSI escape codes (main.rs:218-222, 238-244)**

No check for terminal capability (piping to file, `NO_COLOR` env var, Windows terminal compatibility). When output is piped, the ANSI codes will be visible garbage.

**11. `export_agent_trace` swallows serialization errors (agent_trace.rs:91)**

```rust
serde_json::to_string_pretty(&trace).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".to_string())
```

Silently returning `{}` on serialization failure makes debugging difficult. Since this is called from a CLI command (not a hook), it should propagate the error.

**12. Duplicate `ContributorType` string mapping in `agent_trace.rs`**

Lines 59-64 manually map `ContributorType` variants to strings, duplicating the `as_str()` method already on `ContributorType` in `provenance.rs`. Use `rec.contributor_type.as_str().to_string()` instead.

---

### Low Priority

**13. Custom hex module in `attestation.rs` (lines 107-121)**

The `hex` crate is widely used and battle-tested. A custom implementation adds maintenance burden and potential for subtle bugs (though the current implementation looks correct).

**14. `whoami()` function uses env vars (provenance.rs:381-385)**

`USER`/`USERNAME` env vars can be spoofed by the calling process. For provenance integrity, consider using OS-level identity APIs. Acceptable for Phase 1 but worth noting for hardening.

**15. Missing `#[derive(PartialEq)]` on `ProvenanceRecord`**

This prevents easy equality comparison in tests. Minor but would improve test ergonomics.

---

### Positive Observations

1. **Fail-open pattern correctly implemented**: `let _ = capture_provenance(...)` at line 455 ensures provenance errors never block Claude Code tool execution. The `CODEFLOW_PROVENANCE=0` opt-out is clean.

2. **Proto schema changes are additive-only**: New fields use tag numbers 9-12 on `Event`, all optional. Existing serialized events remain valid. The `// Versioning contract` comment in the proto file is a good practice.

3. **SQLite WAL mode + busy_timeout**: Correctly handles concurrent access from multiple hook processes.

4. **Snapshot upsert with `INSERT OR REPLACE`**: Clean handling of the diff-on-next-PreToolUse pattern state management.

5. **Ed25519 key generation uses `OsRng`**: Cryptographically secure random source. Good choice of `ed25519-dalek` with no unsafe code.

6. **Test coverage is thorough**: 30+ new tests covering record/query/snapshot CRUD, detect_changes, attestation sign/verify, agent trace export, and edge cases.

7. **Clean module separation**: `content_hash` / `attestation` / `provenance` / `agent_trace` are well-factored with minimal coupling.

---

### Recommended Actions (prioritized)

1. **[CRITICAL]** Fix the `&rec.code_hash[..12]` panic -- use `.len().min(12)` or `.get(..12).unwrap_or(&rec.code_hash)`.
2. **[CRITICAL]** Fix `load_or_generate` TOCTOU race with atomic file creation (`create_new`).
3. **[HIGH]** Add Windows ACL protection for signing key, or error out instead of storing unprotected.
4. **[HIGH]** Remove `/tmp` fallback for key storage -- fail with an error instead.
5. **[MEDIUM]** Avoid double file read in `detect_changes` -- compute line count from the same buffer used for hashing.
6. **[MEDIUM]** Respect `NO_COLOR` / detect non-TTY in blame output.
7. **[LOW]** Unify `ContributorType` string mapping to avoid drift between `provenance.rs` and `agent_trace.rs`.

### Metrics
- Type Coverage: 100% (Rust -- all types explicit)
- Test Coverage: 113 tests pass, new modules have comprehensive unit tests
- Linting Issues: 0 (compiles clean)

### Unresolved Questions
- Is there a plan to bridge `provenance::ContributorType` and `proto::ContributorType` for the sync pipeline? Currently provenance records exist only in local SQLite and are not emitted as proto events.
- What is the intended key rotation story? Currently there is no mechanism to rotate the Ed25519 key, and old signatures would become unverifiable if the key file is manually deleted.</result>

# CODEFLOW — AI Code Supply Chain OS

## Overview

Transform RTK (`D:/code/invesments/tools_decisions/rtk-analysis/`) from a token compression CLI into an **AI Code Supply Chain Operating System** answering 4 questions: WHO wrote it, WHAT did it cost, IS it safe, CAN you prove it.

**Codebase reality check:** RTK is 105 .rs files, ~69K LOC. Key assets to extend:
- `tracking.rs` (1689 LOC) — SQLite tracking, RTK compression savings (NOT LLM API tokens)
- `ccusage.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` — Claude Code spending data parsing (actual API billing — authoritative cost source)
- `hooks/hook_cmd.rs` (1126 LOC) — **PreToolUse-ONLY** hooks for Claude/Cursor/Copilot/Gemini. Each invocation = separate OS process. No PostToolUse exists. Payload: `tool_name` + `tool_input.command` only — no model_id.
- `discover/rules.rs` (935 LOC) — static command-rewrite table (`RtkRule` maps CLI → RTK proxies). NOT an extensible rule engine.
- `build.rs` (66 LOC) — **already exists** (Windows stack size + TOML filter concatenation). Must extend, not create.
- `filters/` — 59+ TOML-based output filters

**What does NOT exist yet:** protobuf schema, provenance records, signed attestation, PostToolUse hooks (must be built from scratch), budget policy engine, dependency validation, compliance exports.

**Descoped:** Cloud backend (Go + ClickHouse + NATS + Next.js) moved to separate future plan — too large for this plan's scope. Phase 6 replaced with lightweight CLI export + optional SQLite-based dashboard.

**Target:** 10-week MVP across 7 phases. Phases 1-5 = CLI (Rust). Phase 6 = CLI export + lightweight dashboard. Phase 7 = Launch.

## Brainstorm Source

`brainstorm-final-260606.md` — 3-session brainstorm, verified sources, competitive analysis of 12 competitors, 4-pillar architecture.

## Phases

| Phase | Name | Status | Effort | Dependencies |
|-------|------|--------|--------|--------------|
| 1 | [Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core](./phase-01-foundation-proto-schema-provenance-core.md) | **Complete** | 2w | None |
| 2 | [Cost Attribution Engine](./phase-02-cost-attribution-engine.md) | **Complete** | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 3 | [Budget Governance + Policy Engine](./phase-03-budget-governance-policy-engine.md) | **Complete** | 1.5w | Phase 2 |
| 4 | [Quality Gate — Dependency + Hallucination Detection](./phase-04-quality-gate-dependency-hallucination-detection.md) | **Complete** | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 5 | [Compliance Export Engine](./phase-05-compliance-export-engine.md) | **Complete** | 2w | Phases 1-4 |
| 6 | [CLI Export + Lightweight Dashboard](./phase-06-cloud-backend-dashboard.md) | **Complete** | 1.5w | Phase 5 |
| 7 | [OSS Polish + Launch Prep](./phase-07-oss-polish-launch-prep.md) | **Complete** | 1w | Phase 6 |

**Parallelism:** Phases 2-3 (cost) and Phase 4 (quality) can run in parallel after Phase 1.

## Key Architecture Decisions

1. **Protobuf for events** — structured, versionable, language-neutral
2. **Ed25519 for attestation** — fast, small signatures, no certificate infra needed
3. **Single SQLite DB (extend tracking.db)** — no split-brain risk; single WAL, single retention, single backup
4. **Agent Trace v0.1.0 compat** — implement spec for Cursor/Devin/Cloudflare/Vercel interop
5. **blake3 for content hashing** — fastest cryptographic hash, already in Rust ecosystem
6. **PostToolUse must be built** — only PreToolUse exists; provenance capture via git-diff analysis on PreToolUse + file-system watcher fallback
7. **ccusage is authoritative cost source** — tracking.rs compression tokens ≠ API tokens; new CostRecord is attribution metadata, ccusage is billing truth
8. **Warn/Block only** — no model Downgrade verdict (hook protocol doesn't support model_id in response)
9. **Cross-platform key storage** — use `dirs::data_dir()` (dirs crate already in deps), not Linux-only `~/.local/share/`
10. **Verify name availability early** — check `codeflow` on crates.io, npm, Homebrew, domain before Phase 1

## Risk Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Hook API changes (Claude Code, Cursor) | Multi-agent support already in RTK; abstract hook interface |
| Protobuf adds build complexity | Use `prost` crate; extend existing build.rs (DO NOT create new) |
| Ed25519 key management | Auto-generate per-machine via `dirs::data_dir()` (cross-platform) |
| SQLite concurrency under heavy sessions | WAL mode; single connection (no pooling — tracking.rs uses single conn) |
| PostToolUse doesn't exist | Git-diff provenance capture on PreToolUse of NEXT tool call; file watcher fallback |
| model_id not in hook JSON | Enrich from ccusage session data retroactively; fallback "unknown" |
| Budget enforcement bypassable | Document as local-first limitation; real enforcement requires API key proxy (future cloud) |

## Dependencies

- `prost` + `prost-build` — protobuf for Rust
- `ed25519-dalek` — Ed25519 signatures
- `blake3` — content hashing
- `ureq` — HTTP client (already in Cargo.toml)
- `serde_json` — JSON (already in Cargo.toml)

# Phase 2: Cost Attribution Engine

## Overview

Attribute every token to a specific session → PR → feature. Extend existing `tracking.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` with PR linkage, model pricing lookup, and cost-per-PR calculations. Add `codeflow cost` CLI command.

## Requirements

- Functional: link sessions to PRs via git branch metadata; calculate dollar cost per session/PR/feature; model pricing table (updatable); `codeflow cost` command shows cost breakdown by PR/dev/project
- Non-functional: cost calculation adds <1ms per event; pricing table updatable without recompile; backward-compatible with existing tracking.db

## Architecture

**Critical constraint:** No PostToolUse hook exists. Cost data comes from ccusage (actual API billing), not hook-captured tokens.

```
ccusage CLI (actual Anthropic billing) → parsed by ccusage.rs
    ↓
+ `codeflow cost sync` → import ccusage sessions into tracking.db cost_records
+ Extract PR ref from: git branch name, commit message, env vars (GH_PR_NUMBER)
+ Match session timestamps to PR activity windows
    ↓
CostRecord { session_id, model_id, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag, source: "ccusage" }
    ↓
SQLite (extend tracking.db with cost_records table)
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_COST → queued for export
```

**Existing assets to extend:**
- `ccusage.rs` — **authoritative cost source** — parses actual Anthropic API billing data
- `cc_economics.rs` — computes cost-per-token from ccusage (billing truth)
- `session_cmd.rs` — session analysis for adoption metrics

**IMPORTANT — dual cost system clarification (Finding #4, #8):**
- `tracking.rs` tracks RTK **compression** tokens (input string size vs filtered output size), NOT LLM API tokens. Do NOT use tracking.rs token counts for cost calculation.
- `ccusage` provides actual API billing data — this is the authoritative cost source.
- New `CostRecord` table provides **attribution metadata** (which PR/feature/dev consumed cost), NOT billing truth. Attribution links ccusage billing data to PRs, not a parallel cost system.

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/core/tracking.rs` — add cost_records table, PR linkage fields
- Modify: `src/analytics/cc_economics.rs` — integrate per-PR cost rollups
- Modify: `src/analytics/session_cmd.rs` — add cost column to session analysis
- Modify: `src/analytics/mod.rs` — export cost module
- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — extract PR ref in PreToolUse (no PostToolUse exists), store as session metadata
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `cost` subcommand
- Create: `src/analytics/cost_cmd.rs` — `codeflow cost` command
- Create: `src/core/pricing.rs` — model pricing table + lookup
- Create: `src/core/pr_linker.rs` — git branch → PR linkage logic
- Create: `data/model-pricing.toml` — default pricing table (updatable)

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create `data/model-pricing.toml`**
   ```toml
   [models.claude-opus-4]
   input_per_mtok = 15.0
   output_per_mtok = 75.0
   cache_read_per_mtok = 1.5
   cache_write_per_mtok = 18.75

   [models.claude-sonnet-4]
   input_per_mtok = 3.0
   output_per_mtok = 15.0
   # ... etc for GPT-4o, Gemini, Codex
   ```

2. **Create `src/core/pricing.rs`**
   - Load from `data/model-pricing.toml` (bundled) or `~/.config/rtk/model-pricing.toml` (user override)
   - `fn cost_for_tokens(model_id: &str, input: u64, output: u64, cache_read: u64, cache_write: u64) -> f64`
   - Fallback: if model_id unknown, use median pricing + log warning

3. **Create `src/core/pr_linker.rs`**
   - `fn detect_pr_ref() -> Option<String>` — try in order:
     1. Env var `GH_PR_NUMBER` or `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER`
     2. Parse git branch name: `feat/PROJ-123-description` → `PROJ-123`
     3. Parse recent commit messages for `(#123)` pattern
     - **REMOVED:** `gh pr view` — network call (500ms+) violates <1ms NFR, cannot run in hook hot path
   - `fn detect_feature_tag() -> Option<String>` — from branch prefix or git tag

4. **Extend tracking.db schema**
   - New table: `cost_records (id, session_id, model_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag, project_path, developer_id, timestamp)`
   - Migration: add table if not exists (backward-compatible)

5. **Extend `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`** (PreToolUse ONLY — no PostToolUse exists)
   - In PreToolUse: detect PR ref via pr_linker.rs (env vars + branch name only — no network calls)
   - Store PR ref as session metadata in tracking.db for later ccusage matching
   - Cost calculation happens in `codeflow cost sync`, NOT in the hook hot path

6. **Create `src/analytics/cost_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow cost` — summary of costs for current project
   - `codeflow cost --by pr` — cost breakdown by PR
   - `codeflow cost --by dev` — cost breakdown by developer
   - `codeflow cost --by model` — cost breakdown by model
   - `codeflow cost --by day` — daily cost trend
   - `codeflow cost --pr 1234` — specific PR cost detail
   - `codeflow cost --json` — machine-readable output
   - Reuse display_helpers.rs formatting patterns

7. **Extend `src/analytics/cc_economics.rs`** (authoritative cost source)
   - Add `fn cost_per_pr(tracker: &Tracker, pr_ref: &str) -> PeriodEconomics`
   - Add PR column to economics table output
   - **Clarify ownership:** cc_economics = billing truth (from ccusage). CostRecord = attribution (which PR/feature). Never show two conflicting cost numbers to user.

8. **Wire into main.rs** — add `Cost` variant to Commands enum

9. **Tests**
   - Unit: pricing lookup (known model → expected cost), pr_linker (branch patterns)
   - Integration: mock ccusage import → verify CostRecord in DB with correct cost_usd and PR attribution
   - CLI: `codeflow cost --by pr` with fixture data
   - 12+ new tests

## Success Criteria

- [x] Model pricing table covers Claude (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku), GPT-4o, Gemini (5 models)
- [x] PR linkage detects PR ref from all 3 methods (env vars, branch name, commit message)
- [x] `codeflow cost` shows total cost for current project with breakdown
- [x] `codeflow cost --by pr` shows per-PR cost ranking
- [x] Cost records stored in separate cost.db, backward-compatible (no tracking.db changes)
- [x] Existing `rtk economics` command still works (2079 tests, 0 regressions)
- [x] 36 new tests for pricing (8), pr_linker (10), cost_store (9), cost_cmd (6), plus 3 integration

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Model pricing changes frequently | LOW | TOML file updatable; CLI flag `--update-pricing` fetches latest |
| PR detection fails in detached HEAD CI | MEDIUM | Fallback to "unknown" PR; CI env vars as primary source |
| tracking.db migration breaks existing data | MEDIUM | ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN; test migration path |

10	# Phase 4: Quality Gate — Dependency + Hallucination Detection
11	
12	## Overview
13	
14	Pre-commit quality enforcement for AI-generated code. Detect hallucinated dependencies, vulnerable patterns, and license risks. `codeflow gate` command for CI/CD integration. Can run in parallel with Phases 2-3 since it only depends on provenance data from Phase 1.
15	
16	## Requirements
17	
18	- Functional: detect hallucinated npm/PyPI/crates.io packages; scan AI code for vulnerability patterns; license compliance; `codeflow gate` as CI/CD pre-merge check; `codeflow scan` for ad-hoc scanning
19	- Non-functional: scan <10s for typical PR (~500 LOC); offline mode (cache registry data); exit code 0/1 for CI
20	
21	## Architecture
22	
23	```
24	codeflow gate (or pre-commit hook)
25	    ↓
26	1. Identify AI-generated files (from provenance DB, Phase 1)
27	    ↓
28	2. Extract dependencies: parse import/require/use statements
29	    ↓
30	3. Validate against registries:
31	   npm:      GET https://registry.npmjs.org/{pkg}
32	   PyPI:     GET https://pypi.org/pypi/{pkg}/json
33	   crates.io: GET https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/{pkg}
34	    ↓
35	4. Scan code patterns (NEW quality rules module — discover/rules.rs is a static command-rewrite table, NOT extensible):
36	   - Known vulnerability patterns (regex-based)
37	   - Suspicious API usage (eval, exec, child_process)
38	   - Hardcoded secrets
39	    ↓
40	5. QualityEvent { check_type, severity, file_path, finding, blocked }

# Phase 4: Quality Gate — Dependency + Hallucination Detection

## Overview

Pre-commit quality enforcement for AI-generated code. Detect hallucinated dependencies, vulnerable patterns, and license risks. `codeflow gate` command for CI/CD integration. Can run in parallel with Phases 2-3 since it only depends on provenance data from Phase 1.

## Requirements

- Functional: detect hallucinated npm/PyPI/crates.io packages; scan AI code for vulnerability patterns; license compliance; `codeflow gate` as CI/CD pre-merge check; `codeflow scan` for ad-hoc scanning
- Non-functional: scan <10s for typical PR (~500 LOC); offline mode (cache registry data); exit code 0/1 for CI

## Architecture

```
codeflow gate (or pre-commit hook)
    ↓
1. Identify AI-generated files (from provenance DB, Phase 1)
    ↓
2. Extract dependencies: parse import/require/use statements
    ↓
3. Validate against registries:
   npm:      GET https://registry.npmjs.org/{pkg}
   PyPI:     GET https://pypi.org/pypi/{pkg}/json
   crates.io: GET https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/{pkg}
    ↓
4. Scan code patterns (NEW quality rules module — discover/rules.rs is a static command-rewrite table, NOT extensible):
   - Known vulnerability patterns (regex-based)
   - Suspicious API usage (eval, exec, child_process)
   - Hardcoded secrets
    ↓
5. QualityEvent { check_type, severity, file_path, finding, blocked }
    ↓
Exit code: 0 (pass) | 1 (blocked findings) | 2 (error)
```

## Related Code Files

- ~~Modify: `src/discover/rules.rs`~~ — NOT a rule engine, it's a static command-rewrite table. Quality rules built from scratch in new modules.
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `gate` and `scan` subcommands
- Create: `src/core/quality_gate.rs` — orchestrator: runs all checks, aggregates findings
- Create: `src/core/dep_validator.rs` — dependency existence validation against registries
- Create: `src/core/hallucination_detector.rs` — AI-specific hallucination patterns
- Create: `src/core/license_checker.rs` — license compliance scanning
- Create: `src/cmds/gate_cmd.rs` — `codeflow gate` CI/CD command
- Create: `src/cmds/scan_cmd.rs` — `codeflow scan` ad-hoc command
- Create: `data/quality-rules.toml` — configurable quality thresholds
- Create: `data/top-packages-npm.txt` — top 1000 npm packages for typosquat Levenshtein comparison
- Create: `data/top-packages-pypi.txt` — top 1000 PyPI packages
- Create: `data/top-packages-crates.txt` — top 1000 crates.io packages

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create `src/core/dep_validator.rs`**
   - Parse import statements per language:
     - JS/TS: `import ... from 'pkg'`, `require('pkg')`
     - Python: `import pkg`, `from pkg import ...`
     - Rust: `use pkg::...` (check Cargo.toml deps)
     - Go: `import "pkg"` (check go.mod)
   - Registry validation (existence + reputation — existence alone misses typosquats):
     - `fn validate_npm(pkg: &str) -> ValidationResult` — GET registry JSON, check download count + age + known-malicious via OSV.dev
     - `fn validate_pypi(pkg: &str) -> ValidationResult` — GET JSON, check download count + first published date
     - `fn validate_crates(pkg: &str) -> ValidationResult` — GET API, check download count + age
   - Cache results in SQLite (package_name → exists/not_found, checked_at)
   - Rate limiting: max 10 req/s per registry
   - Offline mode: cache only, warn on miss

2. **Create `src/core/hallucination_detector.rs`**
   - Non-existent API methods on well-known libraries
   - Fabricated URL endpoints
   - Typosquat detection: Levenshtein distance against **bundled top-1000 packages allowlist per ecosystem** (npm, PyPI, crates.io). Without this allowlist, Levenshtein has nothing to compare against.
   - Integrate with OSV.dev API for known-malicious package detection
   - Severity: critical (known-malicious or definitely hallucinated), high (likely hallucinated or typosquat), medium (suspicious)

3. **Create `src/core/license_checker.rs`**
   - Extract license from registry metadata (npm `license`, PyPI classifiers)
   - Flag copyleft (GPL, AGPL) in permissive-licensed projects
   - Configurable allowed/denied lists in `quality-rules.toml`

4. **Create `src/core/quality_gate.rs`**
   - Orchestrator: runs dep_validator + hallucination_detector + license_checker
   - `fn run_gate(files: &[PathBuf], config: &QualityConfig) -> GateResult`
   - `struct GateResult { findings: Vec<Finding>, passed: bool, stats: GateStats }`
   - Blocking threshold: configurable (default block on critical+high)

5. **Create `src/cmds/gate_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow gate` — scan staged files (git diff --staged)
   - `codeflow gate --all` — scan all AI-generated files in project
   - `codeflow gate --pr <ref>` — scan files changed in PR
   - `codeflow gate --json` — machine-readable CI output
   - Exit codes: 0 = pass, 1 = blocked, 2 = error

6. **Create `src/cmds/scan_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow scan <file>` — ad-hoc scan of specific file
   - `codeflow scan --deps` — dependency-only
   - `codeflow scan --security` — security-only

7. **Create `data/quality-rules.toml`**
   ```toml
   [thresholds]
   block_on = ["critical", "high"]
   warn_on = ["medium", "low"]

   [licenses]
   denied = ["GPL-3.0", "AGPL-3.0"]
   allowed = ["MIT", "Apache-2.0", "BSD-2-Clause", "BSD-3-Clause", "ISC"]

   [registries]
   cache_ttl_hours = 24
   offline_mode = false
   ```

8. **Wire into main.rs** — add `Gate` and `Scan` variants

9. **Tests** — 15+ tests covering dep_validator (mock HTTP), hallucination_detector, license_checker, gate_cmd exit codes

## Success Criteria

- [x] Hallucinated npm/PyPI/crates.io packages detected via registry validation + typosquat detection
- [x] Registry results cached in SQLite (dep_cache.db) with configurable TTL
- [x] `codeflow gate` blocks PRs with critical/high findings (exit code 1)
- [x] `codeflow gate --json` outputs CI-compatible JSON
- [x] License compliance flags copyleft in permissive projects (LicenseViolation check type)
- [x] Offline mode works with cached registry data (cache-only, warn on miss)
- [x] 32 new tests (dep_validator 6, hallucination_detector 7, license_checker 5, quality_gate 6, gate_cmd 3, scan_cmd 3, misc 2)

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Registry rate limits in CI | MEDIUM | Aggressive caching (24h TTL); batch requests; respect 429 |
| False positives on valid but rare packages | MEDIUM | Allowlist in quality-rules.toml; `--ignore <pkg>` flag |
| Import parsing misses edge cases | LOW | Start with common patterns; iterate |

## Code Review Summary

### Scope
- Files reviewed: 4 new (`pricing.rs`, `pr_linker.rs`, `cost.rs`, `cost_cmd.rs`), 2 modified (`lib.rs`, `main.rs`)
- LOC: ~590 new lines
- Focus: Phase 2 Cost Attribution Engine

### Overall Assessment
Solid implementation that follows existing codebase patterns well. Build passes cleanly, all 140 existing + 27 new tests pass (167 total). The code is well-structured and modular. I found one **critical** bug, two **high** issues, and several medium items.

---

### Critical Issues

**1. `show_pr_detail()` does not filter by PR -- returns all data (cost_cmd.rs:116-148)**

```rust
fn show_pr_detail(store: &CostStore, pr_ref: &str, json: bool) -> Result<()> {
    let normalized = if pr_ref.starts_with('#') { ... };
    let groups = store.by_group("model", None, None)?;    // <-- ignores PR
    let breakdown = store.by_group("model", None, None)?;  // <-- same call, still ignores PR
```

The `--pr` flag is advertised but the function calls `by_group("model", None, None)` twice, never filtering by `pr_ref`. The `normalized` variable is computed but never used in a query. This means `codeflow cost --pr 123` shows **all cost data across all PRs**, which is both incorrect output and a potential data leak if users rely on it for per-PR attribution.

The comment on line 126 acknowledges this: "This is a simplified version; the full implementation would filter by PR." This should either be implemented or the `--pr` flag should be removed from the CLI to avoid silently returning wrong data.

**Fix:** Add a `by_pr()` method to `CostStore` that filters `WHERE pr_ref = ?`, or add a `filter` parameter to `by_group()`.

---

### High Priority

**2. `normalize_model_id` date-suffix stripping is fragile -- can mangle valid model names (pricing.rs:112-121)**

```rust
fn normalize_model_id(id: &str) -> String {
    let id = id.split(':').last().unwrap_or(id);
    let parts: Vec<&str> = id.rsplitn(2, '-').collect();
    if parts.len() == 2 && parts[0].len() == 8 && parts[0].chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
        parts[1].to_string()
    } else {
        id.to_string()
    }
}
```

The heuristic "last segment after `-` is 8 digits" will incorrectly strip suffixes from model IDs that happen to end with an 8-digit number that is not a date. Example: a hypothetical model `custom-12345678` would be reduced to `custom`.

More importantly, `rsplitn(2, '-')` splits on the **last** hyphen, so `claude-opus-4-20250514` splits into `["20250514", "claude-opus-4"]` which works. But `gpt-4o-mini-20250101` would split to `["20250101", "gpt-4o-mini"]` -- this works too. The risk is low in practice given current model naming conventions, but the function should validate the numeric suffix looks like a plausible date (year 2020-2030 range) rather than any 8-digit number.

**3. `CostStore` is not thread-safe -- `Connection` is `!Send` (cost.rs:23-25)**

```rust
pub struct CostStore {
    conn: Connection,
}
```

`rusqlite::Connection` is `!Send` and `!Sync`. Currently the `CostStore` is created and used within a single function scope in `cost_cmd.rs`, so this is fine. But the struct is `pub` in the core library, and if any future consumer tries to share it across threads (e.g., in the sync daemon or a web handler), it will fail at compile time. This is a design consideration rather than a runtime bug -- the existing `TrackingDb` and `ProvenanceStore` have the same pattern, so it's consistent. Worth noting in docs.

---

### Medium Priority

**4. `summary()` uses `?2 = ?2` trick -- always true, defeats any future query planner optimization (cost.rs:130)**

```rust
query = "SELECT ... FROM cost_records WHERE timestamp_ms >= ?1 AND ?2 = ?2";
```

This is a code smell. The `?2 = ?2` clause is a no-op tautology used to keep parameter count consistent. It's functionally correct but confuses the query planner and makes the code harder to reason about. The `by_group()` method handles this more cleanly with separate SQL strings. Consider using the same if/else pattern in `summary()`.

**5. Prefix matching in `resolve()` iterates HashMap -- nondeterministic order (pricing.rs:92-95)**

```rust
for (key, pricing) in &self.models {
    if model_id.starts_with(key) || normalized.starts_with(key) {
        return pricing;
    }
}
```

`HashMap` iteration order is nondeterministic. If two keys are prefixes of the input (e.g., `claude` and `claude-sonnet`), which one matches first is undefined. In the current bundled table this collision doesn't occur because all keys are distinct enough. But with user-provided TOML overrides, overlapping prefixes could produce inconsistent results across runs. Consider sorting keys by length (longest first) for most-specific-match-wins semantics, or use a `BTreeMap`.

**6. `whoami()` in `cost_cmd.rs` duplicates identity logic (cost_cmd.rs:198-203)**

The developer identity is derived from `USER`/`USERNAME`/`LOGNAME` env vars. If the user is authenticated via `codeflow login`, their identity is likely stored elsewhere (the `auth` module). Using env vars means two developers on a shared machine with the same OS user would be indistinguishable. Not a bug per se, but worth aligning with the existing auth identity if available.

**7. No `LIMIT` on `by_group` results (cost.rs:156-166)**

The `by_group` query has no `LIMIT` clause. For `--by session` on a long-running project, this could return thousands of rows, filling the terminal. The existing `stats.rs` `top_commands` uses `LIMIT 10`. Consider adding a default limit or a `--limit` CLI flag.

**8. `cleanup()` retention logic is inverted -- `cutoff_ms(Some(retention_days))` subtracts from now (cost.rs:218-225)**

```rust
pub fn cleanup(&self, retention_days: i64) -> Result<u64> {
    let cutoff_ms = cutoff_ms(Some(retention_days));
    let changes = self.conn.execute(
        "DELETE FROM cost_records WHERE timestamp_ms < ?1",
```

This is actually correct -- records older than `retention_days` ago are deleted. Not a bug, just verifying the logic since deletion is irreversible.

---

### Low Priority

**9. Compiled regex on every call in `pr_linker.rs` (pr_linker.rs:43, 56)**

`Regex::new()` is called each time `from_branch_name()` or `from_recent_commits()` is invoked. These patterns are static and should use `lazy_static!` or `std::sync::LazyLock` (Rust 1.80+) for compile-once semantics. The performance impact is negligible for a CLI tool but it's a code quality issue.

**10. `cost_cmd.rs` duplicates `format_number` and `truncate` from `stats.rs`**

Both `cost_cmd.rs` and `stats.rs` define identical `format_number()` and `truncate()` helper functions. These should be extracted to a shared utility module (e.g., `crate::fmt` or into `codeflow_core::util`). Not a functional issue but violates DRY.

---

### Positive Observations

- SQLite pragmas (WAL mode, busy_timeout=5000, synchronous=NORMAL) match existing patterns in `tracking.rs` and `provenance.rs` exactly
- Schema migration for stale databases is handled gracefully -- checks for missing columns and recreates the table
- The `by_group` column mapping uses a closed match statement, eliminating SQL injection risk despite using `format!`
- Index coverage is good: session_id, project_dir, pr_ref, timestamp_ms all indexed
- Error handling consistently uses `anyhow::Result` throughout
- The clap Command/Subcommand pattern matches existing Blame/Stats/Cache patterns
- Empty-state handling in `cost_cmd::show()` provides helpful guidance to the user
- Tests are thorough with 27 new tests covering pricing resolution, PR detection patterns, and CRUD operations

### Acceptance Criteria Checklist

|---|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Pricing table covers 5 models | PASS -- Claude Opus/Sonnet/Haiku, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro |
| 2 | PR linkage from 3 methods | PASS -- env vars, branch name regex, commit message regex |
| 3 | `codeflow cost` shows total | PASS |
| 4 | `codeflow cost --by pr` works | PASS |
| 5 | Separate cost.db, backward-compatible | PASS -- uses `data_dir()/cost.db` |
| 6 | Existing tests pass (140/140) | PASS |
| 7 | 27 new tests | PASS |

### Recommended Actions (Priority Order)

1. **[CRITICAL]** Fix or remove `--pr` flag. The `show_pr_detail()` function returns unfiltered data. Either implement a PR-filtered query or remove the flag to prevent misleading output.
2. **[HIGH]** Consider sorting prefix matches in `resolve()` by key length descending for deterministic longest-match behavior, especially with user overrides.
3. **[MEDIUM]** Extract `format_number()` and `truncate()` to shared utility module.
4. **[MEDIUM]** Add `LIMIT` to `by_group` query or a `--limit` CLI flag.
5. **[LOW]** Use `LazyLock`/`lazy_static` for compiled regex patterns in `pr_linker.rs`.

### Unresolved Questions

- Is there an integration point planned where `capture_provenance()` (in `handle_pre_tool_use`) will automatically write cost records? Currently cost tracking requires manual `codeflow cost record` calls -- there's no automatic path from hooks to `cost.db`. The plumbing exists but the bridge between provenance capture and cost recording is not wired up in this phase.

fn show_pr_detail(store: &CostStore, pr_ref: &str, json: bool) -> Result<()> {
    let normalized = if pr_ref.starts_with('#') { ... };
    let groups = store.by_group("model", None, None)?;    // <-- ignores PR
    let breakdown = store.by_group("model", None, None)?;  // <-- same call, still ignores PR
```

The `--pr` flag is advertised but the function calls `by_group("model", None, None)` twice, never filtering by `pr_ref`. The `normalized` variable is computed but never used in a query. This means `codeflow cost --pr 123` shows **all cost data across all PRs**, which is both incorrect output and a potential data leak if users rely on it for per-PR attribution.

The comment on line 126 acknowledges this: "This is a simplified version; the full implementation would filter by PR." This should either be implemented or the `--pr` flag should be removed from the CLI to avoid silently returning wrong data.

**Fix:** Add a `by_pr()` method to `CostStore` that filters `WHERE pr_ref = ?`, or add a `filter` parameter to `by_group()`.

---

### High Priority

**2. `normalize_model_id` date-suffix stripping is fragile -- can mangle valid model names (pricing.rs:112-121)**

```rust
fn normalize_model_id(id: &str) -> String {
    let id = id.split(':').last().unwrap_or(id);
    let parts: Vec<&str> = id.rsplitn(2, '-').collect();
    if parts.len() == 2 && parts[0].len() == 8 && parts[0].chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
        parts[1].to_string()
    } else {
        id.to_string()
    }
}
```

The heuristic "last segment after `-` is 8 digits" will incorrectly strip suffixes from model IDs that happen to end with an 8-digit number that is not a date. Example: a hypothetical model `custom-12345678` would be reduced to `custom`.

More importantly, `rsplitn(2, '-')` splits on the **last** hyphen, so `claude-opus-4-20250514` splits into `["20250514", "claude-opus-4"]` which works. But `gpt-4o-mini-20250101` would split to `["20250101", "gpt-4o-mini"]` -- this works too. The risk is low in practice given current model naming conventions, but the function should validate the numeric suffix looks like a plausible date (year 2020-2030 range) rather than any 8-digit number.

**3. `CostStore` is not thread-safe -- `Connection` is `!Send` (cost.rs:23-25)**

```rust
pub struct CostStore {
    conn: Connection,
}
```

`rusqlite::Connection` is `!Send` and `!Sync`. Currently the `CostStore` is created and used within a single function scope in `cost_cmd.rs`, so this is fine. But the struct is `pub` in the core library, and if any future consumer tries to share it across threads (e.g., in the sync daemon or a web handler), it will fail at compile time. This is a design consideration rather than a runtime bug -- the existing `TrackingDb` and `ProvenanceStore` have the same pattern, so it's consistent. Worth noting in docs.

---

### Medium Priority

**4. `summary()` uses `?2 = ?2` trick -- always true, defeats any future query planner optimization (cost.rs:130)**

```rust
query = "SELECT ... FROM cost_records WHERE timestamp_ms >= ?1 AND ?2 = ?2";
```

This is a code smell. The `?2 = ?2` clause is a no-op tautology used to keep parameter count consistent. It's functionally correct but confuses the query planner and makes the code harder to reason about. The `by_group()` method handles this more cleanly with separate SQL strings. Consider using the same if/else pattern in `summary()`.

**5. Prefix matching in `resolve()` iterates HashMap -- nondeterministic order (pricing.rs:92-95)**

```rust
for (key, pricing) in &self.models {
    if model_id.starts_with(key) || normalized.starts_with(key) {
        return pricing;
    }
}
```

`HashMap` iteration order is nondeterministic. If two keys are prefixes of the input (e.g., `claude` and `claude-sonnet`), which one matches first is undefined. In the current bundled table this collision doesn't occur because all keys are distinct enough. But with user-provided TOML overrides, overlapping prefixes could produce inconsistent results across runs. Consider sorting keys by length (longest first) for most-specific-match-wins semantics, or use a `BTreeMap`.

**6. `whoami()` in `cost_cmd.rs` duplicates identity logic (cost_cmd.rs:198-203)**

The developer identity is derived from `USER`/`USERNAME`/`LOGNAME` env vars. If the user is authenticated via `codeflow login`, their identity is likely stored elsewhere (the `auth` module). Using env vars means two developers on a shared machine with the same OS user would be indistinguishable. Not a bug per se, but worth aligning with the existing auth identity if available.

**7. No `LIMIT` on `by_group` results (cost.rs:156-166)**

The `by_group` query has no `LIMIT` clause. For `--by session` on a long-running project, this could return thousands of rows, filling the terminal. The existing `stats.rs` `top_commands` uses `LIMIT 10`. Consider adding a default limit or a `--limit` CLI flag.

**8. `cleanup()` retention logic is inverted -- `cutoff_ms(Some(retention_days))` subtracts from now (cost.rs:218-225)**

```rust
pub fn cleanup(&self, retention_days: i64) -> Result<u64> {
    let cutoff_ms = cutoff_ms(Some(retention_days));
    let changes = self.conn.execute(
        "DELETE FROM cost_records WHERE timestamp_ms < ?1",
```

This is actually correct -- records older than `retention_days` ago are deleted. Not a bug, just verifying the logic since deletion is irreversible.

---

### Low Priority

**9. Compiled regex on every call in `pr_linker.rs` (pr_linker.rs:43, 56)**

`Regex::new()` is called each time `from_branch_name()` or `from_recent_commits()` is invoked. These patterns are static and should use `lazy_static!` or `std::sync::LazyLock` (Rust 1.80+) for compile-once semantics. The performance impact is negligible for a CLI tool but it's a code quality issue.

**10. `cost_cmd.rs` duplicates `format_number` and `truncate` from `stats.rs`**

Both `cost_cmd.rs` and `stats.rs` define identical `format_number()` and `truncate()` helper functions. These should be extracted to a shared utility module (e.g., `crate::fmt` or into `codeflow_core::util`). Not a functional issue but violates DRY.

---

- SQLite pragmas (WAL mode, busy_timeout=5000, synchronous=NORMAL) match existing patterns in `tracking.rs` and `provenance.rs` exactly
- Schema migration for stale databases is handled gracefully -- checks for missing columns and recreates the table

# CODEFLOW — AI Code Supply Chain OS

## Overview

Transform RTK (`D:/code/invesments/tools_decisions/rtk-analysis/`) from a token compression CLI into an **AI Code Supply Chain Operating System** answering 4 questions: WHO wrote it, WHAT did it cost, IS it safe, CAN you prove it.

**Codebase reality check:** RTK is 105 .rs files, ~69K LOC. Key assets to extend:
- `tracking.rs` (1689 LOC) — SQLite tracking, RTK compression savings (NOT LLM API tokens)
- `ccusage.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` — Claude Code spending data parsing (actual API billing — authoritative cost source)
- `hooks/hook_cmd.rs` (1126 LOC) — **PreToolUse-ONLY** hooks for Claude/Cursor/Copilot/Gemini. Each invocation = separate OS process. No PostToolUse exists. Payload: `tool_name` + `tool_input.command` only — no model_id.
- `discover/rules.rs` (935 LOC) — static command-rewrite table (`RtkRule` maps CLI → RTK proxies). NOT an extensible rule engine.
- `build.rs` (66 LOC) — **already exists** (Windows stack size + TOML filter concatenation). Must extend, not create.
- `filters/` — 59+ TOML-based output filters

**What does NOT exist yet:** protobuf schema, provenance records, signed attestation, PostToolUse hooks (must be built from scratch), budget policy engine, dependency validation, compliance exports.

**Descoped:** Cloud backend (Go + ClickHouse + NATS + Next.js) moved to separate future plan — too large for this plan's scope. Phase 6 replaced with lightweight CLI export + optional SQLite-based dashboard.

**Target:** 10-week MVP across 7 phases. Phases 1-5 = CLI (Rust). Phase 6 = CLI export + lightweight dashboard. Phase 7 = Launch.

## Brainstorm Source

`brainstorm-final-260606.md` — 3-session brainstorm, verified sources, competitive analysis of 12 competitors, 4-pillar architecture.

## Phases

| Phase | Name | Status | Effort | Dependencies |
|-------|------|--------|--------|--------------|
| 1 | [Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core](./phase-01-foundation-proto-schema-provenance-core.md) | **Complete** | 2w | None |
| 2 | [Cost Attribution Engine](./phase-02-cost-attribution-engine.md) | **Complete** | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 3 | [Budget Governance + Policy Engine](./phase-03-budget-governance-policy-engine.md) | **Complete** | 1.5w | Phase 2 |
| 4 | [Quality Gate — Dependency + Hallucination Detection](./phase-04-quality-gate-dependency-hallucination-detection.md) | **Complete** | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 5 | [Compliance Export Engine](./phase-05-compliance-export-engine.md) | **Complete** | 2w | Phases 1-4 |
| 6 | [CLI Export + Lightweight Dashboard](./phase-06-cloud-backend-dashboard.md) | **Complete** | 1.5w | Phase 5 |
| 7 | [OSS Polish + Launch Prep](./phase-07-oss-polish-launch-prep.md) | **Complete** | 1w | Phase 6 |

**Parallelism:** Phases 2-3 (cost) and Phase 4 (quality) can run in parallel after Phase 1.

## Key Architecture Decisions

1. **Protobuf for events** — structured, versionable, language-neutral
2. **Ed25519 for attestation** — fast, small signatures, no certificate infra needed
3. **Single SQLite DB (extend tracking.db)** — no split-brain risk; single WAL, single retention, single backup
4. **Agent Trace v0.1.0 compat** — implement spec for Cursor/Devin/Cloudflare/Vercel interop
5. **blake3 for content hashing** — fastest cryptographic hash, already in Rust ecosystem
6. **PostToolUse must be built** — only PreToolUse exists; provenance capture via git-diff analysis on PreToolUse + file-system watcher fallback
7. **ccusage is authoritative cost source** — tracking.rs compression tokens ≠ API tokens; new CostRecord is attribution metadata, ccusage is billing truth
8. **Warn/Block only** — no model Downgrade verdict (hook protocol doesn't support model_id in response)
9. **Cross-platform key storage** — use `dirs::data_dir()` (dirs crate already in deps), not Linux-only `~/.local/share/`
10. **Verify name availability early** — check `codeflow` on crates.io, npm, Homebrew, domain before Phase 1

## Risk Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Hook API changes (Claude Code, Cursor) | Multi-agent support already in RTK; abstract hook interface |
| Protobuf adds build complexity | Use `prost` crate; extend existing build.rs (DO NOT create new) |
| Ed25519 key management | Auto-generate per-machine via `dirs::data_dir()` (cross-platform) |
| SQLite concurrency under heavy sessions | WAL mode; single connection (no pooling — tracking.rs uses single conn) |
| PostToolUse doesn't exist | Git-diff provenance capture on PreToolUse of NEXT tool call; file watcher fallback |
| model_id not in hook JSON | Enrich from ccusage session data retroactively; fallback "unknown" |
| Budget enforcement bypassable | Document as local-first limitation; real enforcement requires API key proxy (future cloud) |

## Dependencies

- `prost` + `prost-build` — protobuf for Rust
- `ed25519-dalek` — Ed25519 signatures
- `blake3` — content hashing
- `ureq` — HTTP client (already in Cargo.toml)
- `serde_json` — JSON (already in Cargo.toml)
